title: Plaque Assay
description: Segment or reuse plaque masks, quantify plaque count and area per image, and write summary, statistics, and object-detail tables to a results database.
objectives: Choose between segmenting plaque fields and reusing existing labeled masks.
Review the six settings categories without confusing model thresholds with downstream measurement.
Run plaque quantification and verify the resulting SQLite tables and per-image counts.
prerequisite: Prepare TIFF plaque-assay images; for mask reuse, place identically named labeled TIFF masks in the masks subfolder.

scenes.narration: Plaque Assay detects and quantifies cleared host-cell regions. The settings are on the left; the console records resolved settings, progress, output paths, warnings, and errors. The chat box below the console can discuss that context when AI is enabled, but it does not change settings unless you apply a suggested change.

scenes.narration: Model contains the expected plaque diameter. Match this scale to representative plaques and the model's training geometry; a cell-sized value is generally inappropriate for plaque fields.

scenes.narration: Detection Thresholds groups candidate probability, flow consistency, rescaling, resampling, and hole filling. These settings affect new segmentation; they do not alter the precomputed masks reused in this demonstration.

scenes.narration: Image Geometry controls resizing to the dimensions expected by the bundled plaque model. The mask is scaled back to the original field before area is reported, so measurement remains in original pixels.

scenes.narration: Background and Denoising controls background removal and the signal-to-noise anchor used during normalization. Tune it on representative control and treatment wells before a full segmentation run.

scenes.narration: Output and Runtime controls saving, GPU batch size, and verbosity. Reduce batch size if segmentation exceeds available memory; keep verbose logging for the first plate so resolved paths and behavior are recorded.

scenes.narration: When segmenting, probability controls the candidate floor, flow threshold controls shape consistency, and Fill in closes interior holes. Inspect multiple wells because a value that cleans one plaque can merge or erase another.

scenes.narration: Click Run after reviewing the modified settings. This demonstration measures four synthetic labeled masks through the real plaque-analysis backend; it does not present the synthetic fields as biological validation of the segmentation model.

These four fields contain four, three, two, and one plaques respectively; use the per-image counts and areas with your plate metadata for downstream condition-level statistics and quality control.
